In eukaryotic cells, a network of fine fibres forms the cytoskeleton, which provides structural support, maintains cell shape, and enables cell movement and internal transport. It is visible only under an electron microscope as a separate entity. The cytoplasm may also store starch (in plant cells), or crystals of calcium oxalate or silica (in some plant cells). These are known as cell inclusions.

Viruses, viroids, and prions are acellular (no cells) infectious agents that are too small to be seen under a light microscope. Viruses are composed of some genetic material with a protein coat. Viroids lack protein coat around its genetic material, while prions are misfolded proteins which lack genetic material.
